stops.note: starch from the pith of the sago palm, a staple food in the Moluccas and New Guinea; Antonio Pigafetta, chronicler of Magellan's voyage, recorded sago bread in the Moluccas in 1521
arrived through Portuguese traders' accounts; sago pudding later became a fixture of Victorian nursery food

current_meaning: a starch from the pith of the sago palm, used in puddings
